measure: HB 2198 (repeal of data center sales tax exemption)
summary: House voted 197-5 to repeal the exemption. The Senate passed repeal language in a separate bill, HB 1667 (44-6). Neither version reached the governor.

measure: HB 1834 (PUC regulation of commercial data centers)
summary: Would require the PUC to assign connection, transmission, network upgrade, reliability, and PJM emergency capacity costs to data centers. Referred to Senate Consumer Protection and Professional Licensure on March 31, 2026.

measure: HB 2496 (municipal pause on data center applications)
status: Passed House; cleared Senate committee; awaits Senate vote
summary: Passed the House 201-1 on June 24, 2026, and the Senate Local Government Committee 11-0 on June 30. Would let municipalities adopt, by resolution, a pause of up to 180 days on data center applications while they update ordinances, usable once every three years. Sponsored by Rep. Paul Friel.

measure: Executive Order 2026-05 (GRID Requirements)
summary: DEP reviews data center permit applications only with a legally binding commitment to the GRID Requirements, made through a Consent Order and Agreement for projects above 25 MW peak demand, and will not issue permits until local land use approvals are secured. Developers who decline face a delayed track: DEP will not begin review until all local approvals are in place. Revenue must update exemption guidelines so new applicants comply with GRID. Bars Commonwealth agencies under the governor's jurisdiction from entering nondisclosure agreements related to data center projects; local governments are not covered (HB 2359, pending, addresses local NDAs). Requires a public map of proposed projects and directs DEP to collect annual energy and water use data from existing facilities.

measure: FY 2026-27 Fiscal Code (SB 146, Act 21 of 2026): energy and water reporting
summary: Enacted July 12, 2026 in the FY 2026-27 Fiscal Code (SB 146, Act 21 of 2026), originally HB 2150. Data centers with peak electric demand of at least 10 MW must report energy and water use annually to the Department of Environmental Protection, which will publish the data, starting in 2027.

measure: PUC model large-load tariff (Docket M-2025-3054271)
summary: Statewide model tariff framework for customers over 50 MW individually or 100 MW in aggregate. Each electric distribution company implements it through a utility-specific tariff subject to PUC approval.

measure: FY 2026-27 Fiscal Code (SB 146, Act 21 of 2026): load forecast oversight
summary: Amends Act 45 of 2025 to authorize the PUC's enforcement bureau and statutory advocates to review utility agreements and customer commitments that affect load forecasts submitted to PJM.

measure: HB 2775 (grid interconnection before local zoning approval)
summary: Cleared a House committee unanimously the week of Sept. 28, 2026. Would require data centers to apply for grid interconnection before seeking local zoning approval.

measure: HB 2674 (no public utility status for data centers)
summary: Cleared a House committee unanimously the week of Sept. 28, 2026. Would bar data centers from obtaining public utility status.

measure: HB 2828 (large-load tariff adoption; emergency curtailment)
summary: Cleared the House Energy Committee unanimously. Would require utilities to adopt the PUC's large-load tariff and data centers to curtail use during grid emergencies.

measure: SB 1408 (ban on data center NDAs with state agencies and local governments)
summary: Cleared the Senate Communications and Technology Committee unanimously. Would ban nondisclosure agreements between data center developers and both state agencies and local governments.

measure: 2026 biennial budget (HB 30): sales tax exemption
summary: Budget kept the data center sales and use tax exemption. The Joint Subcommittee on Tax Policy must study the exemption and report by mid-December 2026.

measure: 2026 biennial budget (HB 30): electricity consumption tax
summary: New tax of $0.011 per kWh on data center electricity, capped at $600 million a year with excess refunded pro rata. Expires June 30, 2028 absent extension.

measure: Large-load cost allocation (25 MW and above)
summary: Costs of increased generating capacity assigned to customers with 25 MW or more of demand. HB 284 directs two utilities to create voluntary demand flexibility programs for those customers.

measure: HB 153 / SB 94: siting and pre-vote disclosure (Va. Code 15.2-2209.5)
summary: Governs where the largest facilities can go and what developers must disclose before a local board votes.

measure: SB 253: backup generator air permits
summary: DEQ may not issue air permits for data center generators applied for on or after July 1, 2026 unless they meet Tier IV or an equivalent standard.

measure: Water use and reporting
summary: Water reporting authority takes effect January 1, 2027. DEQ cooling water scarcity area regulations due July 1, 2027. Budget also requires data centers to limit water use for cooling.

measure: SCC annual data center report
summary: SCC's first annual report reported about 21,800 MW of contracted data center demand and 13,767 permitted backup generator sets, about three-quarters of them Tier 2 or older. It reported electricity and generator data but no water data; municipal utility responses are pending, and DEQ's public water-use dashboard goes live January 1, 2027.

measure: NextEra acquisition of Dominion Energy
status: Under SCC review; evidentiary hearing begins Nov. 17
summary: The SCC is reviewing NextEra's proposed acquisition of Dominion Energy, which would carry a 130 GW large-load pipeline. The evidentiary hearing begins Nov. 17, 2026.

measure: Data Center Accountability Framework and Executive Order 22
summary: Framework on local approval transparency, energy costs, and environmental standards. EO 22 implements core pieces and creates an AI Task Force.

measure: Carried-over bills
summary: Of 61 data center bills considered in 2026, 15 went to the governor and 46 carry over to 2027.

measure: Pause on new sales tax exemption requests
summary: Governor DeWine directed the Tax Credit Authority to pause consideration of new data center exemption requests while the Joint Data Center Committee studies data center growth.

measure: AEP Ohio data center tariff
summary: PUCO-approved tariff requires new data centers to pay for at least 85% of the load they request. The Ohio Manufacturers' Association is challenging it at the Ohio Supreme Court.

measure: House bill extending the AEP tariff approach statewide
summary: Bipartisan bill (Reps. Thomas and Rader) modeled on the AEP tariff.

measure: Senate data center bill (rate class; NDAs; water; local impacts)
summary: Would create a PUCO data center rate class and address tax breaks, nondisclosure agreements, water use, and local government impacts.

measure: Substitute HB 646 (exemption cut; rate class; PUCO tariff)
summary: Would cut new sales tax exemptions from 100% to 50%, create a data center electric rate class, and require a data center tariff at the PUCO. Stalled in June when the House and Senate lacked the votes to pass it. No data center bill has been enacted.

measure: HB 975 / SB 374 (repeal of sales tax exemption)
summary: Bills to repeal the data center sales tax exemption remain in committee without hearings.

measure: Utility RELIEF Act of 2026
summary: Defines large load customers for tariff purposes, requires data centers to pay for the infrastructure and grid costs they create, and requires confidential reporting aggregated into an annual public report.

measure: Executive Order 01.01.2026.16
summary: Single state review for projects of 25 MW or more; new Data Center Task Force and public dashboard. Agencies defer substantive review until local land use approvals are documented; state incentives require alignment with state principles; agencies may not enter NDAs with data center developers.

measure: PSC large load tariff proceeding
summary: BGE, Pepco, and Delmarva large load tariffs are before the Public Service Commission.

measure: County moratoriums and bans
summary: 14 of 24 jurisdictions have moratoriums or bans (Daily Record count). Harford County passed the first indefinite ban in June; Frederick County extended its pause to July 1, 2027.

measure: Repeal of 2020 sales and use tax exemption
summary: Governor Moore will seek repeal in the 2027 General Assembly session.

measure: Sales tax exemption repeal and pause bills
summary: The Senate passed a repeal bill on March 6. The session ended with the exemption intact. SB 436 (suspend new certificates) and HB 1012 (construction pause) were introduced.

measure: HB 1063 (utility contracts with data centers)
summary: Passed the House 159-5. Did not become law.

measure: PSC large-load rules and generation approval
summary: Customers of 100 MW or more must take service under custom contracts. In December 2025 the PSC approved nearly 10,000 MW of new generation, roughly 80% expected to serve data centers. Base rates frozen through 2028.

measure: Customer Identified Resource program
summary: Lets large customers, including data centers, fund their own clean energy projects for bill credits, up to 3 GW through 2035.

measure: County moratoriums
summary: Numerous counties adopted data center moratoriums in 2026 while they write zoning rules, including Cobb County (adopted February, extended six months in August; the county noted its 1972 zoning code gives no consideration to data centers), Dougherty County (extended 180 days in August), Cherokee County (July), and Fannin County (extended through Dec. 31, 2026).

measure: Public Service Commission elections
summary: Two PSC seats on the ballot, with data center regulation a key campaign issue.
